new_statements.quote: [Singh 2003, 2.0] In Purum language there are three major sound systems. They are vowels, consonants and tone. These sound systems consist of six vowels phonemes, nineteen consonant phonemes and two tones. ... [2.4 TONE, p. 39] In Purum, there are two tones. They are falling and rising tones. The falling tone is marked (\) and rising tone is unmarked. Example 83. kə̀y 'I' kəy 'to pull' ... 85. sìn 'small' sin 'work' 86. wòk 'pig' wok 'to hit' ... [LSI 1904 III/III p. 263, Purum, Pronunciation] An accented final vowel is probably long, but is shortened when the stress is transferred to another syllable. ... We have, however, no information as to where the stress should come

new_statements.rule_in_words: Purum is described as a two-tone language (falling vs rising lexical tone, contrastive on monosyllabic roots); the only modern phonology available (Singh 2003 ch. II) has no stress or accent section and never mentions stress, and the only source that uses the word 'stress' (LSI 1904) says explicitly that where it falls is unknown. No word-stress placement rule exists in any reachable description.
new_statements.exceptions: None (no stress rule stated). LSI 1904 notes final accented vowels shorten 'when the stress is transferred to another syllable' but gives no rule.
new_statements.domain_note: Tone is lexical, illustrated on monosyllabic and sesquisyllabic (mə-, ə- prefixed) citation forms; no word- or phrase-level stress domain is discussed. Meitei 2021 (Tezpur CFEL volume, pp. 88-109, not online) is reported by its editors to also posit two lexical tones.
new_statements.identity_note: puru1262 is a Glottolog BOOKKEEPING languoid for the retired ISO 639-3 code [puz] 'Purum Naga'. ISO 639-3 Change Request 2013-008 (adopted 2014-02-03; file, p.2 sec. 4) merged [puz] into [pub] Purum on the ground that 'Both the languages have the same information on location and Population in most available resources. So it seems to be one language.' The living languoid is puru1266 Purum [pub], which is ALREADY in the catalog (verdict TONAL, Singh 2003). All descriptive sources (Singh 2003, Meitei 2021, LSI 1904, Das 1945) are about that one Purum; there is no separate 'Purum Naga' variety with its own description. This key should be recorded as a duplicate of puru1266, not as a new catalog entity (retired codes confer no identity). Side note seen in a Crossref record: a 2007 genetics paper titles the group 'Purum (Chothe)', reflecting a view that Das's 1945 Purum villages are today's Chothe; Singh 2003 and the Tezpur CFEL project treat Purum (Senapati district villages) as its own language.

sources.note: The only modern dedicated phonology of Purum (22 pp., CFEL fieldwork with recordings); covers phonemes, syllables and two lexical tones per the editors and is the one place a statement on stress/prominence (or its absence) beyond Singh 2003 could exist. Online PDF at tezu.ernet.in/wmcfel/pdf/ is front matter only.
